name: Bran Castle
description: Famous medieval castle, commonly known as Dracula's Castle. Built in 1377, it's one of Romania's most iconic landmarks.

name: Palace of Parliament
description: The world's second-largest administrative building after the Pentagon. A massive example of totalitarian architecture.

name: Peleș Castle
description: Neo-Renaissance castle built between 1873-1914 as a summer residence for King Carol I. Located in the Carpathian Mountains.

name: Corvin Castle
description: Gothic-Renaissance castle, one of the largest in Europe. Built in the 15th century, it's considered one of the most beautiful castles in the world.

name: Sighișoara Citadel
description: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Best-preserved inhabited medieval citadel in Europe, birthplace of Vlad the Impaler.

name: Transfăgărășan Highway
description: Spectacular mountain road crossing the Carpathian Mountains. Built in the 1970s, it's one of the most scenic drives in the world.

name: Voroneț Monastery
description: UNESCO World Heritage Site, famous for its vibrant blue frescoes. Built in 1488, it's known as the 'Sistine Chapel of the East'.

name: National Museum of Art of Romania
description: Main art museum in Romania, housed in the former royal palace. Contains extensive collections of Romanian and European art.

name: Turda Salt Mine
description: Ancient salt mine converted into a stunning underground tourism destination. Features an amphitheater, Ferris wheel, and underground lake.

name: Curtea de Argeș Monastery
description: Beautiful 16th-century monastery, masterpiece of Byzantine-Romanian architecture. Contains royal tombs.
address: Strada Negru Vodă 27, Curtea de Argeș 115300

name: Danube Delta
description: UNESCO World Heritage Site. Europe's second-largest river delta, home to over 300 species of birds and 45 species of fish.

name: Merry Cemetery
description: Unique cemetery famous for its colorful tombstones with naive paintings describing the deceased's life in a humorous way.

name: Brașov Old Town
description: Medieval city center surrounded by Carpathian peaks. Features Gothic, Baroque, and Renaissance architecture.

name: Black Church (Biserica Neagră)
description: Largest Gothic church in Romania, built between 1385-1477. Named after fire damage in 1689.

name: Romanian Athenaeum
description: Concert hall in Bucharest, headquarters of the Romanian Philharmonic. Iconic neoclassical building opened in 1888.

name: Viscri Fortified Church
description: UNESCO World Heritage Site. 13th-century fortified church in a traditional Saxon village, promoted by King Charles III.

name: Bicaz Gorges
description: Spectacular canyon carved by the Bicaz River through the Carpathians. Popular destination for hiking and rock climbing.

name: Alba Carolina Fortress
description: Largest Vauban-style fortress in Romania, built in 18th century. Site of the 1918 Union of Transylvania with Romania.

name: Mamaia Beach
description: Romania's most popular beach resort on the Black Sea coast. 8km long sandy beach with modern facilities.

name: Village Museum (Muzeul Satului)
description: Open-air museum showcasing traditional Romanian village life. Features over 300 authentic peasant farms and houses.
